page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It has no local storage or GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.c5.2xlarge generally falls into the lower performance tiers for raw compute and memory operations. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, along with Geekbench scores, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. However, it achieves average performance in Passmark CPU and extended instruction tests, as well as in large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth. It also demonstrates average performance for small-model LLM inference prompt processing and text generation, though performance drops to the bottom 10% for larger models.

Given its compute-focused resource density and moderate network throughput, this instance is suited for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have modest memory and storage requirements. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, basic batch processing, and small-scale application hosting. The lack of local storage and lower benchmark scores relative to higher-tier instances suggest it is a cost-efficient option for non-critical compute tasks where high memory capacity or extreme IOPS are not required.
